“I don’t know either. Seeing Doma and the Geomjon together around you, I just thought I should jump in too. Though I didn’t expect to end up saying all this.”

“Do you feel better now that you’ve said it all?”

“I’m already regretting it. Why did I have to reveal such pathetic deeds with my own mouth? Like I was possessed by a ghost. Completely caught up in that talk about half-purity or whatever.”

He flopped down on the floor. And looking blankly up at the pavilion ceiling, he spoke.

“You’ll think of this every time you see me from now on.”

“I suppose I will. Sigh, our pathetic older brother.”

At my words, Chwima laughed. The small laugh gradually grew bigger. After a refreshing bout of laughter, he asked.

“Will you reveal the truth to those two?”

I shook my head.

“That’s not for me to decide.”

“I intend never to reveal it to them, though?”

“Do that.”

“You’ll really let me do that.”

“Please do.”

Chwima sprang up and looked at me.

“Don’t you want those two to reconcile?”

“Would those two truly be happier knowing the truth?”

“!”

“Setting aside hatred for you, those two would grieve even more that their love failed for such a reason. Because it cannot be turned back, that regret would only grow. Can those two start a new love now? Is that possible? In the end, all three of you would become more miserable than you are now.”

I think it is a truth that must be buried forever. Hyeolcheon Doma might fly into a rage and try to kill Chwima. Even if he killed Chwima, Hyeolcheon Doma would pay the price as well. And what of the Geomjon’s heart in the midst of that? After all, this happened because Chwima liked her.

“Think of it as using up your one chance to reveal the truth on me right now.”

There will be a great difference between whether you told me or not. Because this past that clings like a specter is not something one can face alone.

“If you free yourself from the obsession that the truth must be revealed, you might instead reconcile the two better. Starting now, try to get closer to Hyeolcheon Doma, and when drinking with the Geomjon, offer praise instead of slander. Then wouldn’t an opportunity to connect those two arise unexpectedly someday? Give them wings even now.”

“You should be the older brother.”

“I refuse. If I’m going to tease our pathetic older brother, it’s more fun if he’s the older brother.”

Chwima’s expression became much more at ease. Having said everything, he looked relieved.

“Do keep one promise.”

“What is it?”

“Cut down on drinking, and eat your snacks. Since it’s come to this, we have to let our pathetic older brother live a long life.”

I don’t know if Chwima’s fate will change with today as a turning point. Even with this, whether he’ll eventually die of drink, or live a different life.

Perhaps changing his fate will make him die even earlier. But that’s fine. Any death is better than the final moments of Chwima dying from alcoholism.

“Hyung, let’s have one last drink. I can’t drink anymore. And…… thank you for being honest with me.”

The expression with which he looked at me was something I had never seen before. Can we truly maintain this expression toward each other until the very end?

“Little brother…… thank you.”

Chwima toasted toward my cup.

* * *

The next day, Father called for me.

When I entered the Heavenly Demon Hall, I sensed the atmosphere was different from usual.

Grand Strategist Sama Myeong was there, and my older brother Geom Muyang was present as well.

After greeting Father and Sama Myeong, Geom Muyang spoke to me.

“You reek of alcohol. The smell of alcohol in a place where you meet Father?”

“I drank a bit too much yesterday. With the person who likes alcohol the most in our sect.”

I deliberately mentioned Chwima. Geom Muyang tried to act composed.

“Yes, I heard you’ve been spending time with Chwima lately. Don’t drink too much.”

Geom Muyang must be feeling displeased. He would have wanted Chwima to come cause problems for me, but instead it must look like the two of us are having a good time.

Even so, Geom Muyang was trying his best not to show his emotions. Truly, my older brother in front of Father becomes a different person.

“Shouldn’t you be more careful, Hyung?”

“What do you mean?”

“I heard you’ve been hanging around with the Poison King these days? Mine is alcohol, but yours is poison, isn’t it? Be careful, Hyung.”

Even in front of Father, a sharp war of nerves unfolded. I deliberately didn’t hide it. From Father, and from my older brother.

As could be seen from Chwima’s case, emotions hidden and hidden again eventually cause problems. Fighting openly like this and engaging in a battle of nerves. This is the right way if I’m going to fight to save my older brother. Because if you’re angry outwardly you curse, but if you’re angry inwardly you send assassins.

Father watched our conversation with an unknowable gaze, then signaled Sama Myeong with a nod.

Then Sama Myeong stepped forward and spoke.

“Today, different missions will be given to the two young masters.”

In Sama Myeong’s hand were two red envelopes.

The inevitable had finally come. The true trial to decide the successor had begun.

“To ensure fairness, please choose whichever one you prefer.”

The moment I saw those envelopes, my heart surged.

Before the regression, today came to mind. The two missions given to us.

My older brother succeeded, and I failed.

By botching this mission, I completely fell away from the successor’s position.

Just as in the past, this time too my older brother gave me the first chance to choose.

“Choose first. Don’t regret it later if you chose wrong.”

“That probably won’t happen.”

Slowly, I reached out my hand and chose one of the two envelopes.

Chapter 141: Make the Right Choice This Time.
---------------------------------------------
I chose the path I knew.

Before the regression, I had chosen the mission on the right, and today, too, I chose the envelope on the right.

I can handle any mission now!

This was not the time to show such confidence. It was an opportunity to humbly make up for my past failure.

Inside the envelope was a single sheet of paper, and four characters were written on it.

Punishment of False Demons (僞魔懲罰).

It was the very order I had been given in the past.

Sima Ming sent me a voice transmission to explain. It was so that neither of us would know the other’s mission.

—Recently, a strange organization called the Tianming Society (天命會) has begun operating in the shadows of the murim. They have raised the banner of creating a new murim under Heaven’s mandate, but in truth they are people seeking private gain. Of late, they have caused several incidents while impersonating the Demon Venerables of our cult, and matters have reached a point where they can no longer be ignored. Second Young Master, find their society leader, execute him, and eliminate the Tianming Society.

In truth, when I heard this voice transmission before the regression, I looked down on them. Not because they had put their skills forward, but because they had gone around impersonating the Demon Venerables of our cult.

But now I took it differently. The fact that they dared impersonate Demon Venerables meant either that they were confident they could handle the consequences, or that some other scheme was hidden behind it. These bastards were not ordinary bastards.

“I shall obey the order.”

Once I accepted my mission, Geom Muyang chose the remaining envelope. Of course, I knew very well what mission was written inside that envelope.

After Sima Ming conveyed the basic information to Geom Muyang by voice transmission as well, he spoke to the two of us.

“You must resolve the mission alone. However, while the two of you are carrying out your missions, you may use all of the information networks of our cult’s Tongtian Pavilion, and you may call upon the Demon Army, the Four Greats of the Demonic Path, or one of the Eight Demon Venerables of your choosing, one time only.”

It meant that while we had to solve it alone, we could receive help from the cult when it came time to subjugate them.

When Sima Ming finished speaking, Father said,

“A frog in a well or a flower in a greenhouse cannot lead our cult. Resolve it properly and return!”

This was my father, who did not offer a single word of caution even while entrusting us with such dangerous missions. I smiled and eased the rigid atmosphere.

“Father, which one of us do you hope returns successful?”

At my question, the corners of Father’s mouth rose slightly. I could sense that he was forcibly holding back something he wanted to say.

In truth, Father’s gaze as he looked down at us was impartial. He did not send either me or my elder brother a personal look.

Before the regression, I had not been looking at Father in this moment. I had been thinking only of completing the mission somehow.

But now, I was looking at Father.

Father, don’t worry. I’ll resolve it safely and come back.

I conveyed that faith with my eyes. This, too, was an effort to become the successor. The more Father trusted me, the closer I would step toward the position of heir.

My gaze, which had been directed at Father, turned to Geom Muyang.

‘Brother, do well and come back like you did before. I’ll do well and come back too. Ah, and don’t look at me so coldly when you don’t even know how I feel.’

* * *

The next morning, as I was preparing to depart, Ian came to see me.

“You called for me?”

“I’ll be leaving the cult for a while and then returning.”

“Where are you going?”

“I can’t tell you.”

I raised a finger and pointed upward. Ian realized that I was leaving to carry out an order handed down from the Heavenly Demon Hall.

“Bring me back something tasty when you return!”

“I’m not going out to play. I’m going to handle something extremely dangerous.”

“I’m busy with martial arts training, so I’ll be going now.”

“Terrifying enemies are going to come pouring out.”

“Have a safe trip!”

Ian, who had run all the way to the door like that, let out a sigh and turned back.

“How nice would it be if I could really leave like this? How dangerous is it? I’ll go with you and help.”

She had changed from Ian joking around to Ian worrying about me day and night.

“It’s something I have to do alone. And I was joking too. You don’t need to worry.”

“Really?”

“Don’t worry for nothing. Just focus on your own work.”

“Actually, Lord Blue Mask came to see me not long ago.”

I had watched the two of them meet, but I pretended not to know.

“Did he say he’d become the squad leader?”

“No, he’s still thinking about it. He just asked me a few things and left.”

“What does your intuition say?”

“Half and half. To be honest, right now I desperately hope he comes, but if he really does, I think I might worry even more. Because he’d be living a new life because of me.”

“Worrying about what comes after is disregarding Blue Mask’s own deliberation. At a glance, it may seem as though you have to take responsibility for him, but that isn’t the case at all.”

“It isn’t?”

“That’s right. Blue Mask will be coming after careful consideration as well. He’ll come because, after working the abacus hard, he judged that coming to you would be more beneficial. If he comes and decides it isn’t right, he’ll go back. So don’t feel burdened.”

At my words, Ian grinned.

“Become strong, Ian. Then nine out of ten problems you’re worrying over will resolve themselves.”

After parting with Ian, I left my residence.

Before leaving, I intended to stop by and see the Demon Venerables one by one. They were people I did not particularly need to look after, but this time, I wanted to see each of them before I went.

The first place I visited was the Extreme Evil Lesser Demon’s Valley of the Wicked.

He had always been in that white room, staring at the wall, but today Blue Mask informed me of his absence.

“The Demon Venerable left the cult several days ago.”

“Can you tell me where he went?”

“He left without telling even me.”

“When he returns, please tell him I stopped by.”

“Yes, I will.”

As I turned to leave, Blue Mask asked me,

“There is one thing I would like to ask.”

“Please speak.”

“You may find this question strange coming out of nowhere, but what kind of organization is the Ghost Shadow Unit to you, Second Young Master?”

Because I knew very well why he was asking this question, I answered honestly.

“It is the organization that will become my main force in the future. It is also the organization led by the person I cherish most. It will probably become the busiest organization in the murim. So much so that you’ll naturally find yourself saying that things were better under the Extreme Evil Lesser Demon.”

I could see the eyes behind Blue Mask’s mask smile.

“Thank you for telling me.”

Blue Mask bowed his head in greeting. I could have said a few words to him for Ian’s sake, but I did not. Only if he judged and decided for himself would even his regrets become worthwhile regrets.

Next, I stopped by the Ilhwa Sword Venerable.

After hearing from the Drunken Demon about what had happened in the past, I found myself thinking about her life at least once.

If things had truly worked out between her and the Blood Heaven Blade Demon, would she have been happier than she was now?

“You seem to have grown even younger these days.”

“Don’t say such nonsense. I’ve been worried lately because I’ve gained so many wrinkles.”

Even as she said that, the Ilhwa Sword Venerable’s face brightened at the rare compliment on her appearance.

“I heard you drank with the Drunken Demon.”

“How did you know?”

“The Drunken Demon came by. He said he’d gotten some good liquor and gave me some. He did something he never usually does.”

“What did he say when he gave you the liquor?”

“He was so proud and pleased, saying that he and you had become sworn brothers.”

“I don’t know if that’s a good thing. If he and I are sworn brothers, the hierarchy of seniority gets all tangled.”

“Then be friends with me as well.”

“Please don’t say such things even as a joke. What I said back then was only a joke.”

The Drunken Demon probably had not come to boast about becoming sworn brothers with me. After confessing everything to me, he must have felt sorry toward her.

How the Drunken Demon would act from here on was something to be seen.

“As you know, the Drunken Demon and the Blade Demon are not on good terms. Will it be all right?”

“You have to help me, Senior.”

“How?”

“Even if you don’t feel inclined, please say good things about Elder Blade Demon too. I know. I know you are displeased with him. But I ask this of you for my sake.”

The Ilhwa Sword Venerable gave no answer. It seemed that even my face was not enough yet to erase her aversion toward the Blade Demon.

Still, I expected things to improve compared to before. If the Drunken Demon stopped speaking ill of the Blood Heaven Blade Demon and began saying positive things, then her feelings toward the Blade Demon might slowly change as well.

Next, I stopped by the Drunken Demon.

But Yeo Bin gave me unexpected news.

“The Drunken Demon has entered closed-door training.”

Because it was so sudden, I was startled.

“Closed-door training all of a sudden?”

“He said he had drunk too much lately and needed to expel some of the wine qi.”

“That’s a good thing, right?”

“Yes. It was something I truly hoped for. Thank you, Second Young Master.”

“Not at all. He promised me that he’d cut down on drinking and eat plenty of food when he drinks, so please take good care of him, Martial Artist Yeo.”

“Yes, I will.”

I had felt it for a long time. This Yeo Bin liked the Drunken Demon. Did the Drunken Demon know of her feelings? I suspected that, like the sly old fox he was, he knew and was pretending not to.

Among the Demon Venerables, the last place I stopped by was the residence of the Blood Heaven Blade Demon.

“Elder, your blade is becoming even fiercer.”

Today, too, the Blood Heaven Blade Demon was immersed in training.

“The more you grow, the fiercer your enemies will become.”

“Are you truly training in order to face my enemies? Do you intend to clash with the Demon Venerables who support my brother?”

“It is not only because of the successor struggle.”

“Then why?”

“Do you remember what I told you before? That when a dragon ascends to the heavens, it brings wind and rain with it.”

“Of course. You said that my people were being swept away by that wind and rain.”

“That’s right. You said you were just a loach stirring up muddy water, but I believe that those waves will awaken the sleeping dragons of the murim.”

“Aren’t you overestimating me too much?”

“Judging by what you have shown so far, even this is an underestimate. Be careful even after you leave. It may seem as though our cult, the Murim Alliance, and the Evil Path Alliance have divided and seized control of the murim, but compared to all martial artists, our numbers are only a small fraction. We do not know where people stronger than us may spring out from. Do not forget. The jianghu is a place where eccentrics and hidden masters are as numerous as grains of sand.”

“I will always judge carefully and move with caution.”

“And, wait a moment.”

The Blood Heaven Blade Demon went into his room and came out carrying a small box. When I opened it, there was a single medicinal pill inside.

“It is a Swift Recovery Pill (速功丹). Use it if you ever find yourself in urgent need.”

The Swift Recovery Pill was a medicinal pill that, when taken after one’s internal energy had been exhausted, allowed one to recover internal energy two or three times faster than usual.

Because it had no side effects, it could only be obtained by paying an enormous sum, and even then, it was so uncommon that it was not easy to find.

“Please keep it and use it yourself, Elder.”

“Are you planning to work this old man so hard that you’ll even make me eat a Swift Recovery Pill? You take it and use it.”

He forced the Swift Recovery Pill into my hand. Feeling his concern and hidden affection for me, my heart swelled.

Elder, don’t worry. I’ll be careful and return safely.

Since I was accepting it anyway, I accepted it in a cheerful mood.

“Is there nothing else you can give me? Please go inside and look for more.”

“There isn’t! There’s nothing left!”

“Seeing how strongly you deny it, there must be something. I’ll look forward to next time.”

I greeted him with a laugh and was about to turn away when the Blood Heaven Blade Demon asked,

“What happened with that sinister fellow?”

“We agreed to be sworn brothers from now on.”

The Blood Heaven Blade Demon first looked dumbfounded, then impressed.

“If you were a loach, you would never have been able to become sworn brothers with that sinister fellow.”

It meant that though he might not like the Drunken Demon, becoming sworn brothers with him was an impressive feat.

“I am doing as I please because I trust you, Elder.”

“And that is why this old body is swinging this heavy blade, is it not?”

After leaving the Blood Heaven Blade Demon’s residence, I left the cult.

Once I reached a deserted place, I began to run in earnest. These days, I had grown to prefer moving alone, if only because of Swift Step.

But even while running, when it was time to rest, I rested properly. My every movement on this mission would be reported to the Heavenly Demon Hall. There was no need to inform everyone that I could run at an unbelievable speed.

I ran while pushing Swift Step to its limit, and once I arrived at a predetermined point, I spent the remaining time there practicing the rest of the Wind God’s Four Steps.

Dark Shadow Step became even more stealthy, Flicker Step became even faster, and Underworld King Step became even more savage. I trained and trained again. I poured in all my effort and concentration. For the time being, my martial arts goal was unconditionally the complete mastery of the Wind God’s Four Steps.

According to the materials sent by the Tongtian Pavilion, the Tianming Society had caused several incidents throughout Hunan.

The two places where recent incidents had occurred were Yongxing (永興) and Dongkou (洞口).

In the past, I had gone to Yongxing and investigated the incident there while tracking the Tianming Society. But in the end, the Yongxing incident turned out not to be the work of the Tianming Society. It had been committed by people imitating the Tianming Society.

Because of that, I wasted a great deal of time in the past, and only belatedly went to Dongkou to follow their traces. As a result, my mind grew impatient, I missed clues I should have found, and in the end I failed the mission.

Of course, this time I made the proper choice.

After arriving in Dongkou, I went straight to Yuefeng Sect (月風門), where the incident had occurred.

Chapter 142: The Answer Lies with You.
--------------------------------------
Chusaeng (秋生), the master of the Wolpung Sect, was struggling to contain his boiling rage.

“Please do not worry too much. Several sects in Hunan have promised to cooperate with us.”

It was precisely such words that angered him. And hearing them from Seok Hyeong, a man he trusted, only made him angrier.

“Cooperate? How? Tell me specifically. How many men did they say they would send, when, and where?”

Seok Hyeong could not answer. They had only said they would help; not a single sect had come forward with such concrete terms. Despite all their efforts to keep it secret, rumors were already spreading that the Demonic Cult had become involved.

“Put yourself in their place. Do you think they would send you to deal with the Demonic Cult bastards? Outwardly, they’ll pretend to be concerned, but they’ll be too busy locking their own doors.”

Chusaeng sprang to his feet. At the force in him, as though he might smash something at any moment, Seok Hyeong tried to stop him.

“Please calm yourself.”

“How am I supposed to endure this when I’m furious? Those Demonic Cult sons of bitches! I’ll chew them alive!”

Boom!

Chusaeng thrust out a palm and punched a hole through the wall. Since the incident had occurred, more than twenty holes had already appeared in the walls. They patched one up, and he broke through another; patched that one, and another was broken.

Chusaeng felt so wronged and enraged he could hardly bear it. He could not contain the fury rising within him. And at the root of all those emotions was fear.

Fear that the bastard would return.

Chusaeng could not sleep at night, and his nerves had grown strained to the utmost.

“Even now, you should ask the Murim Alliance for help.”

The Wolpung Sect had originally been a sect that stood between the righteous and unorthodox paths, belonging neither to the Murim Alliance nor the Evil Dao Alliance.

“If I do that, we’ll be at the mercy of the Murim Alliance bastards from now on. If they resolve this matter, they’ll use it as an excuse to force us to obey the Murim Alliance unconditionally. And even if they fail to resolve it, they’ll use one pretext or another to bring us under their control.”

Sects belonging to the Murim Alliance had to pay a fixed sum to the alliance every year. The same was true of the Heavenly Demon Divine Cult and the Evil Dao Alliance. In return, when trouble arose, they could receive help.

Money was one thing, but Chusaeng did not want to belong to the righteous faction.

It was then that someone spoke his thoughts exactly.

“You wouldn’t want to serve under bastards who do nothing for you in ordinary times and yet never fail to wring money out of you, would you?”

Startled, Chusaeng and Seok Hyeong turned around. At some point, a young man had entered the main hall.

Seok Hyeong stepped between the sect master and the man, drawing his sword.

“Who are you?”

The fact that they had not noticed someone enter like this put both men on edge.

Then the young man said,

“I have come from the Divine Cult.”

The one who had startled the two of them was none other than me.

I could have announced myself from the entrance, but I deliberately did not. At present, the Wolpung Sect was in a chaotic state, with countless martial artists swarming from the gate all the way inside.

“Forgive me. I dislike crowds, so I came in quietly.”

Chusaeng had Seok Hyeong step back. He had acknowledged that if I had intended to ambush them, they would already be dead.

“I am Chusaeng, master of the Wolpung Sect.”

Having lost his father early, he was among the youngest heads of sects in Hunan Province, being in his late twenties.

I did not reveal my identity to him.

“I have come to deal with the incident that occurred in your sect. Circumstances prevent me from revealing who I am, but you should recognize this.”

I showed them the divine token engraved with the evil spirit that symbolized our cult.

Naturally, Chusaeng began with suspicion.

“A divine token can be forged. I cannot trust you on that alone.”

“How did someone as suspicious as you get deceived by them?”

“You go too far!”

Just as Seok Hyeong took a step forward, I stretched out my hand.

Swaaaah.

The demonic energy emitted from me constricted Seok Hyeong’s body.

With a brief groan, he found himself unable to move. As his breath was cut off, his face turned bright red.

“Sometimes, one’s ability can stand in for one’s identity, can it not?”

With the demonic energy dominating the surroundings, Chusaeng spoke urgently.

“Stop! I lost several subordinates this time. I cannot lose another. Release him.”

When I withdrew my demonic energy, Seok Hyeong gasped for breath and was able to move again. He glared at me with fearful eyes, but he still stood in front of Chusaeng to protect him.

“I, too, have loyal subordinates like you. If I were to lose them, I would truly feel as though my heart had been torn out. The same must be true for Sect Master Chu here, so the two of you should not act rashly.”

Though I said it to Seok Hyeong, in truth, it was also meant for Chusaeng. Quick to understand, Chusaeng sent Seok Hyeong out.

“You wait outside.”

“Yes.”

Seeing him leave obediently in this situation, it seemed Chusaeng had sent him a voice transmission. Since the two of them alone could not deal with me anyway, he had likely ordered him to go out and gather all the experts of the Wolpung Sect.

Even after only the two of us remained, Chusaeng was composed.

“You people caused the trouble, and now you come claiming you will clean it up. Just what are your intentions?”

“Not clean it up. Investigate. The previous incident was not our doing.”

Chusaeng snorted. He had been struck by the Cheonmyeong Society, which had impersonated one of our cult’s Demon Venerables, and he firmly believed it was our doing.

Several similar incidents had occurred recently, but not all the sects of the Central Plains were aware of this yet.

In other words, it was still a time before the Cheonmyeong Society had fully surfaced.

“Tell me what happened. If I had come to harm you, would I be standing here trading words like this?”

Perhaps those words reached him, for Chusaeng finally began to speak of the past incident.

“Not long ago, someone came here, claiming to be from the Divine Cult.”

“Who did he say he was?”

“He was Geugak Soma.”

I had known they had impersonated a Demon Venerable, but I had not known the one they chose was Geugak Soma.

A hollow laugh escaped me. Of all people, why would they go around pretending to be Geugak Soma? What did they plan to do if they were caught by the real Geugak Soma?

“What did he look like?”

“He came wearing a white mask.”

Then again, since he wore a mask, Geugak Soma was probably the easiest Demon Venerable to impersonate.

“You believed him just because he wore a mask?”

At that, Chusaeng spoke with conviction.

“He was the real Geugak Soma.”

“Why do you believe that?”

In that instant, Chusaeng was swept up in anger.

“He killed the experts of my sect in an instant. His finger wind pierced holes through their faces, and his palm art shattered their bodies into pieces. Among the dead was one of the top three experts of our sect. If he was not Geugak Soma, then who in the world was he?”

It seemed they had even imitated Geugak Soma’s unique demonic arts, the Mageuk Gwangpokjang and the Hyeorangji. With the situation like that, Chusaeng had no choice but to believe it.

“After killing those who tried to protect me and turning the place into a sea of blood, Geugak Soma forced us to submit to the Demonic Cult and swear loyalty.”

The bastard had committed unnecessary slaughter solely to frighten his opponent. That act alone made him an evil deserving of death.

“And do you know what else he did? It would have been less absurd than this if he had simply massacred us. I would have thought we had just been unlucky enough to run into him and die.”

“What did he do?”

“As he left, he stole our money. He told us to hand over all the money we could provide right then. He cleaned out all the sect’s funds. And yet thieves like you dare—!”

Whatever insult might have followed, it was a situation I could understand.

“How much money did he take?”

“About sixty-two thousand nyang.”

Only then could I understand Chusaeng’s rage. I also understood why there were so many holes in the walls.

“If we had fought for some other reason and lost, I would not feel so wronged. Submit to the Demonic Cult? Don’t make me laugh! That was just an excuse. He killed my subordinates like that so he could steal our money. Do you understand what I am saying? My subordinates died for mere money! If he wanted money, he should have asked for it from the beginning!”

Unable to hold back, he roared.

“Uaaaaaah! I am so furious I cannot endure it. I will not die a natural death.”

Listening to Chusaeng, I thought he must ordinarily have been a pleasant and cheerful person. At this rate, he would never return to who he had been. The families of the dead, their friends, the survivors. The number of victims had yet to be determined.

“Right now, Sect Master Chu, you are so angry that you cannot make use of your strengths.”

“And what exactly are my strengths!”

I took a sheet of paper from my robes and read it.

“Chusaeng, master of the Wolpung Sect. Clear-headed and possesses sound judgment. Strong pride, with a hot-blooded side.”

“What bastard made that assessment?”

“The head of our cult’s Tongcheon Pavilion Hunan branch. Would you like to meet him?”

Chusaeng stared at me with eyes that seemed torn between believing and disbelieving, then rebuked himself in a drained voice.

“What good are a clear head and sound judgment? I was only helplessly victimized like this.”

“Even so, should you not take revenge?”

At the word revenge, strength returned to Chusaeng’s eyes.

“I will. I absolutely will.”

There had been a time when I felt the same.

Revenge when I slept, revenge when I ate, revenge when I looked at people. A time when my mind was filled only with thoughts of how I would take revenge, and I could not live a normal life.

Chusaeng was the same. The enemy before him was not one he could face by ordinary means.

But fortunately, just as I had met Seojin, he had met me.

“I will help you with that revenge.”

Chusaeng went to the table and gulped down the cold tea straight from the pot.

“Was it truly not your doing?”

“Doesn’t something seem strange to you as well? If the real Geugak Soma had been after your money, do you think he would have taken only sixty-two thousand nyang and left? He would have pulled up the very pillars of this place.”

“What if it was merely a kind of amusement?”

“If he enjoyed such amusement, he would die by the hand of the Cult Leader, the Heavenly Demon himself. Let us say it was amusement. If that had been the case, who here would have survived?”

“To be honest, I found it strange as well. That is why I thought Geugak Soma had gone mad.”

If he stared at white walls like that long enough, he might someday go mad.

“He is still sane. I met him not long ago.”

At my words that I had met Geugak Soma, Chusaeng flinched. But because of the ability I had shown him, he did not seem to think I was bluffing.

“Are you saying Geugak Soma is truly in your cult?”

For a moment, I hesitated to answer. When I had set out, Geugak Soma had not been in the Valley of Villains.

“He was.”

I did not answer that way because I wanted to avoid an argument with Chusaeng. It was because I was certain this was not Geugak Soma’s doing. Father says one can never know what is inside another person, but there are still things one can know. No matter how wicked Geugak Soma may be, he is not the kind of person to commit such an act.

“If that man was a fake, then the one in your cult must be fake as well.”

It made me wonder just how overwhelming the figure he had seen had been for him to say such a thing.

I slowly walked around the main hall and looked about. I tried to recall the scene from that time. The scene of the Wolpung Sect’s martial artists being killed and their money stolen.

Why in the world had they done this? For money? Or to draw us in? In this incomprehensible incident, I had to find a clue about them.

“Fine. Let us say he was a fake, as you claim. Then why did that fake bastard do something like this? Was he trying to sow discord with the Murim Alliance? Was he trying to start a war?”

“If that were the case, he would have touched a righteous sect belonging to the Murim Alliance.”

“Then what in the world is going on?”

“That is why I came. To uncover what is going on.”

After staring at me for a while, Chusaeng opened the door and went outside. Outside, Seok Hyeong and dozens of Wolpung Sect martial artists who had gone ahead were waiting in formation.

Chusaeng went out alone and spoke to Seok Hyeong.

“Have all the men withdraw, and clean out a guest room for him. We will be treating him as an honored guest for the time being.”

“Yes, understood.”

Seok Hyeong looked relieved. Though he had gathered the martial artists, he seemed to have judged that they could not handle me.

Chusaeng came back inside.

“The thought that you may be in league with that bastard still will not leave my mind. Even so, I intend to try trusting you. Do you know why? Because right now, I have to grasp at even a straw.”

Then he suddenly looked up at the ceiling and shouted,

“Father! Grandfather! Please help me! Please do not let me be toyed with any longer! Watch over this sect! Save my subordinates!”

Considering his fate had led him to meet me, his ancestors were already helping him plenty.

After shouting once, he revealed his true feelings. He lowered his voice so his subordinates outside would not hear.

“Because you came, I am ruined. If, as you say, he was a fake Geugak Soma, then I cannot stop seeking revenge. If it had been the real Demonic Cult, I might have been able to give up, telling myself there was nothing I could do. Because of you, I have stepped onto a bridge from which I can never return. I will have to cross this endless bridge of revenge for the rest of my life!”

“I will help you cross that bridge.”

In the past, I had arrived too late, and in my urgency, I had left this place without even investigating properly.

In those days, I did not look at Father, and I did not look at Ian. It was a time when I looked only at myself and not at others, so naturally, I did not look at Chusaeng either.

“There are countless sects in murim, yet there must be a reason they chose your sect in particular. Why you? Young, clear-headed, hot-blooded, and proud. Aside from what is written on this paper, what else is there about you?”

I approached him, stared intently into his face, and said,

“There must be a reason they chose you. Now give me the answer!”

Chapter 143: The Reason You Appeared Before Me.
-----------------------------------------------
“If I knew the answer, would I be in this state?”

Chusaeng shouted.

He certainly was hot-blooded. There couldn’t be many people who could shout like this at a demonic practitioner, knowing full well that the other party’s martial arts were far superior to their own.

“My apologies. These days, the vessel of my patience is filled to the brim and sloshing over. Drop so much as a pebble into it and it spills.”

“I understand.”

“What do you understand?”

He flared up again, then soon apologized.

“I’m sorry. This isn’t something I should be taking out on you.”

“It’s all right. In a situation like this, wouldn’t it be stranger to remain calm?”

Chusaeng said to me in a slightly softened tone.

“What should we do now?”

“Do as you normally would. Pretend I’m not here and proceed with whatever you meant to do.”

“How am I supposed to pretend you’re not here when you are?”

“Focus only on yourself. In a situation where your life hangs in the balance, what can’t be done?”

I took out the paper on which information about him was written and handed it to him outright.

“Keep that with you at all times, and when you feel confused or your confidence falters, unfold it and read it. Especially don’t forget the part about you being sharp. You are a sharp man. So use that clever head of yours and judge well.”

Chusaeng clenched the paper he had been reading. It seemed even that paper was about to make his vessel of patience overflow. He could not bring himself to tear it up, and instead tucked the crumpled sheet into his robes.

“How do you intend to move now? If I hadn’t come, would you have sent word to the Murim Alliance?”

At my question, Chusaeng pondered for a moment, then shook his head.

“I would sooner have joined hands with the Sado Alliance than call the Murim Alliance.”

“Then will you join hands with the Sado Alliance?”

“Not them either.”

He was answering honestly. Even before the regression, he had not joined hands with either the Murim Alliance or the Sado Alliance.

“Then how were you planning to resolve this?”

“I don’t know.”

At that very moment, I saw it. The slight tremor in his eyes. To deceive me, he would have to be capable of deceiving even himself, and he was still far too young.

‘So there is something he is hiding from me.’

But I did not pressure him. It was only natural that he would not trust someone he had just met. When the other party is trying to hide something, pressing them only gets you lies or excuses. At times like this, one must respond calmly.

“Let us rest for today.”

* * *

Seokhyeong guided me to the guest room.

Good food and wine were brought out. I checked each dish with a silver needle to see if it had been poisoned, then finished my meal.

Afterward, I trained in the Wind God Four Steps in my room. If the space was narrow, I trained accordingly; if it was wide, I trained accordingly. Training in a room was an extension of the spar I had shared with Father at the inn earlier, so it was highly effective.

Now that I had set the goal of reaching great completion before receiving instruction in the Guhwa Demonic Art, my training would not stop.

* * *

When the moon hung bright and full in the sky, I went to see Chusaeng.

Despite the late hour, he had not fallen asleep and was lost in thought in his room.

“Did you rest well?”

“I rested well, but Sect Master Chu seems not to have slept a wink.”

“I haven’t been sleeping properly lately.”

Indeed, Chusaeng’s eyes were bloodshot red.

“If you cannot sleep, you cannot make proper judgments.”

“What can I do when sleep will not come even if I want it to?”

“Try sleeping properly for even one day. Shall I help you?”

“How? Are you going to press my sleeping acupoint?”

“There is a secret method for falling asleep when sleep won’t come that I learned from our cult’s demon physician.”

At the words that I had learned it from a demon physician, Chusaeng seemed intrigued.

“Now, there’s nothing to lose, so lie down on the bed.”

“This is embarrassing for a grown man.”

Contrary to his words, Chusaeng must have been suffering greatly from his sleeplessness, for he obediently lay down on the bed like a new bride.

“Do as I say. First, relax the muscles of your face. Next, let the tension out of your shoulders and arms. More comfortably. Now, this time, relax your thighs and both legs entirely. And imagine that you are lying on a sandy beach beneath warm sunlight. Good. Then raise a strand of qi from your dantian and slowly move it as I instruct. From the Shuifen acupoint to the Zhongwan acupoint, from Zhongting to the Yutang acupoint, slowly. And then again…”

* * *

When Chusaeng opened his eyes, it was morning.

Awakening on the bed, he was bewildered. He had not slept properly in recent days, yet the throbbing headache was gone, and his body felt light enough to fly. He truly had slept so deeply it was astonishing.

“Ah! That secret method!”

It seemed he had fallen asleep without realizing it while following the method taught to him by that man from the Demon Cult whose name he did not even know.

Chusaeng climbed down from the bed and hurried out of the room.

Geom Mugeuk was in the main hall where they had first met yesterday, staring at the marks on the wall.

“You’ve come?”

“Thanks to you, I slept well. I don’t know how long it’s been since I slept that deeply.”

“Sect Master Chu seems like a man suited to the righteous faction.”

“What are you suddenly talking about?”

“I thought the reason Sect Master Chu couldn’t sleep was because of guilt over failing to protect your subordinates.”

“What nonsense are you spouting? I was simply angry at that man. I couldn’t sleep because I was so furious and resentful I couldn’t master my own temper.”

Chusaeng disliked being treated as part of the righteous faction. This was largely due to his father’s influence. Ever since he was young, his father had taught him that if one was kind, one would be taken advantage of.

“Do you think I could have survived in this jianghu until now with such half-baked feelings? Ridiculous. Don’t irritate me with pointless words.”

“Understood.”

When he accepted it too readily, Chusaeng grew angry in his own way again. He had come to thank him for helping him sleep well, yet for no reason he was only raising his voice.

Then Geom Mugeuk turned and pointed to the wall as he asked.

“This hole here.”

“Ah, I made a few of those because I was angry. I’m on the verge of making another one even now.”

“Not those. This one.”

There was a small hole where Geom Mugeuk pointed.

“Is this the hole made by the finger wind he fired?”

Chusaeng’s expression stiffened.

“That’s right. It pierced through my subordinate and went on to pierce that wall. I deliberately told them not to patch this place. So I could look at it again and again and remember what happened that day.”

Geom Mugeuk’s expression was grave as he looked at the hole.

“What is it?”

“It looks exactly like the real Hyeorang Finger.”

“Are you perhaps referring to the martial art of the Vile Little Demon?”

“That’s right. I have seen his martial arts before.”

At that, Chusaeng grew excited.

“See? Wasn’t I right? It really is the Vile Little Demon!”

“It is not the Vile Little Demon.”

“What are you saying now? Didn’t you say it was the real Hyeorang Finger?”

“I meant that the technique was that profound. It was not the work of the Vile Little Demon.”

“You seem to trust the Vile Little Demon far too much.”

“I do trust him.”

“That is exactly why I trust you even less. How can I trust someone who trusts the Vile Little Demon this much?”

“Whether you trust me or not is your freedom, but trust me this time.”

Chusaeng silently stared at Geom Mugeuk. He was a truly strange person. He said he had come from the Demon Cult, yet he did not feel like a demonic practitioner. He lacked that unique rough, cruel, sinister feeling of a man of the demonic path. Rather, though only a few days had passed since they had met, he had a peculiar power that somehow made one keep wanting to trust him.

‘If this man is evil, he will become a truly great evil.’

Hiding that thought, Chusaeng asked Geom Mugeuk.

“Then why did you tell me, knowing I would suspect you like this?”

“Because I should. Since we decided to join forces, there is nothing more foolish than acting while hiding one’s true thoughts. If we were going to do that, we should not have joined hands in the first place.”

Those words stabbed straight into Chusaeng’s heart, for he was hiding something.

“If you cannot sleep tonight either, use the method I taught you. Your complexion is much better.”

* * *

The next morning as well, Chusaeng came to see me.

“I slept well again yesterday. Perhaps you were right. The better I sleep, the more apologetic I feel toward those who died.”

“Think of the other disciples Sect Master Chu must protect. What can be done? The living must live on and move forward.”

It was a trite consolation, but perhaps it served as comfort nonetheless, for he rose with a somewhat easier expression.

“If there is anything inconvenient, tell me.”

“I will.”

Like someone with something to say, Chusaeng looked around the room here and there.

“How long are you going to stay here? I don’t think anything will change by you remaining like this.”

“Until you tell me the truth.”

“!”

Chusaeng flinched for an instant and turned toward me.

“Because I slept well and my head cleared, my thoughts about you changed too. I thought, there must be a reason that man is staying by my side. Someone so extraordinary would not be here for no reason.”

I spoke to him calmly.

“That’s right. I had noticed that you were hiding something from me.”

Around the time we first met, he would have flatly denied my words. But the Chusaeng of now did not.

“Then why do you not force me? With your martial arts, you could find out even if you had to torture me by force.”

“This may sound strange to you, but I will say it. My demonic path is a demonic path that eliminates the absolute evils of the world. My demonic path does not break tables, and my demonic path does not torture those who are not evildoers.”

“That truly is a strange thing to say.”

But his expression differed from his words. He was beginning to understand, at least a little, what kind of person I was.

“I believe the reason they chose you is because of whatever it is you are hiding right now. If my guess is correct, you will eventually die to them because of it. You may not believe it, but I want to save you.”

“You may not believe it… but I believe your words. There is no reason I should believe you, yet I keep wanting to, and that makes me hesitate even more. I wonder if I am being deceived by you. My father said never to trust another person’s words. That was his dying wish.”

Chusaeng looked up at the sky. What answer was his father giving him now?

He had done well until now, but this trial that had befallen him before he had even reached thirty was too difficult for him to overcome by his own strength.

Tell him to open his heart a little, for your son’s sake. I will make sure your son lives.

Did that thought of mine reach him?

After agonizing for a long while, Chusaeng revealed what was in his heart.

“After this matter occurred, I kept thinking of one method. I continued to agonize over whether I should tell you about it or not. My head told me I must never reveal the secret, but my intuition told me to reveal it. It told me to trust you.”

“I will contact the Hunan branch of Tongcheongak and tell them to change their records about you. His intuition is good, but he is not sharp. Like that.”

Chusaeng laughed. It was the laugh of a man who had now made up his mind.

“I was planning to ask one person for help.”

“Who is that?”

“I do not know who it is either.”

Chusaeng took out something he had kept carefully hanging from the cord of his necklace and showed it to me.

It was a coin cut exactly in half.

“It is an Eunwon Coin.”

An Eunwon Coin was a kind of token made by cutting a coin in half and giving it to a benefactor, so that even if a descendant later brought the coin, the favor would be repaid.

“They say the owner of this Eunwon Coin was injured and hovering between life and death when my father saved him. When he handed this down to me, my father repeatedly admonished me to use it only when my life and the fate of the clan depended on it.”

“Do you know who the owner of this coin is?”

Chusaeng shook his head.

“He did not tell me. I do not even know whether that person is still alive.”

“How is this Eunwon Coin used?”

“He said that if I went to any Yellow River Inn in the Central Plains and showed the coin to the innkeeper, someone would come looking for me.”

Using inns to make contact was a method used by our cult and the Murim Alliance. I thought the owner of the coin was likely someone who had once belonged to a large organization.

“Can anyone take it?”

“No. He said only our direct family line can use it. I am not saying this because I fear you might take mine from me. He truly told me that was the case.”

“I believe you. If that were not so, they would already have killed you and taken the Eunwon Coin.”

“Do you truly think he did such a thing because of this?”

“I cannot be certain, but that is my intuition.”

If, as I expected, this was what they were after, then they must be searching for the owner of this coin. Just who could it be?

“When the incident happened, why did you not use it immediately?”

Chusaeng let out a long sigh.

“I agonized over it. Truly, I agonized until my head felt as if it would burst. I was afraid. I was afraid that if I used this, I would become entangled with that man again. I was afraid that if revenge failed, he would come find us and annihilate our sect. I would rather everything simply pass by like this.”

Chusaeng lifted his head and looked at me.

“I believe you appearing before me was my father sending someone to rebuke me for such cowardice. I will stake my fate and that of my sect on you.”

* * *

Four days later.

We were sitting in a Yellow River Inn in Hunan. When we showed the coin to the innkeeper, he merely told us to wait here.

We waited without any plan.

Perhaps afraid that someone would come and leave without meeting him, Chusaeng sat in the inn all day long.

I shut myself in my room and trained in the Wind God Four Steps, then when mealtime came, I ate with Chusaeng, drank tea, and conversed with him.

I told him about the Heavenly Demon Divine Cult. I also told him stories about famous martial artists, sects, and wandering warriors from various regions, and spoke of scenic wonders and delicious dishes throughout the Central Plains. I taught him about hunting and camping as well.

He marveled at my extensive knowledge. No matter what he asked, I was someone who could answer.

At one point, Chusaeng even said this.

“How can someone so young know all this? Are you perhaps… someone who has returned to youth?”

“Even if I had the chance, I would not do it. I will grow old together with my people and die.”

“I am curious what kind of people they are. Who surrounds a person like you? I want to see them.”

“You will regret it if you do.”

“Why?”

I answered with a smile instead. He would not say such things after being poked in the side by the Blood Heaven Blade Demon until he was bruised black and blue.

On the tenth day of waiting there like that, someone finally came looking for us.

The moment he saw him, Chusaeng was so startled he sprang to his feet.

And not only Chusaeng, but I, too, was shocked.

A man wearing a white mask was striding toward us.

Chapter 144: You Look Even More Handsome in a Mask.
---------------------------------------------------
"It's him! That man right there!"

Qiusheng shouted. Upon seeing the white mask, he was half out of his mind.

"Flee! No, we must flee!"

Perhaps thinking I had frozen in fear, Qiusheng screamed as if having a fit.

"Even you cannot stand against that man! Let us flee at once."

When I remained still, Qiusheng frowned and drew his sword.

"Damn it! Let's attack together!"

I could understand why his father had left a dying wish not to trust people. Even in this situation, he was a man who did not run and looked after my safety.

Before we knew it, the man in the white mask had approached our table.

The white-masked man stared at us silently.

Qiusheng trembled violently. Though he had sworn revenge, now that he faced his opponent, his body would not move as he willed.

When I first saw him, I had naturally assumed he was the fake Ji'e Xiaomo who had come to Yuefengmen.

Ji'e Xiaomo nodded at my words. He clearly seemed to have a guess as to who was behind this.

What he accepted was not the Enyuan Coin's request, but my jest.

Startled by Ji'e Xiaomo's attitude, which said their business was done.

Xuelu Sanjun.

They were once vagabonds who dyed the martial world in terror, accepting any contract as long as money was paid. They killed indiscriminately, women and children alike, and were known to kill even their own parents if paid.

Eventually, their evil deeds became so excessive that they were condemned as public enemies of the martial world and vanished from it, yet today they revealed themselves here.

They had made their notorious names at middle age; now they had grown old. The wickedness they had accumulated through countless trials replaced their diminished muscle. They seated themselves at a table far from us.

Again, a middle-aged woman appeared in the inn, swaying a pink fan. She wore gaudy palace attire with thick makeup, and her figure was voluptuously sensual, as if bursting.

Jile Yaoji.

She was a heinous villainess who had sucked the vital essence of countless men to forge her internal energy. That skin and figure, so ill-suited to her age, had been created by stealing the vital essence and lives of countless men. She too had once ranked first among the public enemies of the martial world. Rumor had it that she had fallen prey to a heinous lecher and died from having her internal energy drained in reverse, yet here she was, brazenly alive.

She revealed her pale legs, crossed them, and sat astride a table.

Next, a middle-aged man entered.

Wearing a single straight blade at his waist, he emanated an air like a beast wandering the wilderness.

Xuelang Dao.

He was the very martial artist who had sought out experts of the Central Plains solely to grow stronger. He did anything to win and forcibly fought even those who wished to avoid combat. Thus, too many experts had died unjustly by his hand.

Eventually, he too was condemned as a public enemy of the martial world, and there were many rumors regarding his end: that he died fighting an elder of the Martial Alliance, that he died challenging a Demon Venerable, that he died at the hands of a nameless hermit expert. The last to appear was a man dressed entirely in black clothes and shoes, with a black cloak wrapped around him.

Yanluo Shenjun.

Though he appeared sane now, he was once a mad martial artist who had massacled martial artists in his insanity. He had believed himself to be a messenger sent by the King of Hell, considering himself a god who governed life and death. He too had been condemned as a public enemy of the martial world, stirring up a storm of blood before disappearing.

Villains who had once shaken the martial world had appeared all at once, so rather, it felt unreal. Moreover, the mastermind behind the impersonation had yet to show himself.

It was not the time to act leisurely, but I could not help saying this to Ji'e Xiaomo.

"Just what on earth have you been doing?"

Looking at the villains radiating killing intent toward him, Ji'e Xiaomo replied sheepishly.

"They are all people I know."

The terrain swarmed with swamps, venomous snakes, and poisonous insects, and all manner of traps had been installed there, so anyone who entered recklessly would lose their life before taking even a few steps inside.

Even if one safely overcame those dangers and made it inside, all kinds of villains awaited within. A child who offered directions would stab your throat with a dagger, and a kindly-looking old woman would put poison in your rice. That was the Valley of Villains.

The Murim Alliance had attempted to subjugate the place several times, but each attempt had failed. There were simply too many villains, and every time, they suffered heavy losses and were forced to turn back.

Even so, there was one reason the Valley of Villains had never become a single force and burst out into the murim.

Because they were villains.

Whenever someone tried to unite them, someone would inevitably betray them. From the moment they opened their eyes, they stole from one another, fought, and killed, making it impossible for them to unite into one faction.

And yet, people from that very Valley of Villains had joined hands for the purpose of killing the Evil Smiling Demon. If the person behind this had moved not ordinary villains, but figures of this caliber, then that alone was enough to guess that the mastermind was truly extraordinary.

When he opened the Ledger of Life and Death, the Evil Smiling Demon’s name was written there in red characters.

The Paradise Enchantress licked her lips with her tongue, coveting the Evil Smiling Demon.

“He may be damn troublesome, but he looks like he’d be delicious.”

The Three Lords of the Blood Road were the same.

“If those ones kill him, we’ll have to keep listening to them boast for the rest of our lives. Let us take the lead.”

It seemed they all wanted to fight the Evil Smiling Demon. Well, to them, killing the Evil Smiling Demon would be something to brag about for a long time.

Seeing that, I said to the Evil Smiling Demon,

“You’re popular.”

“This is nothing. If I go over to the righteous faction, it becomes a complete uproar. The line of people wanting to kill me stretches for ten li.”

At his joke, I burst out laughing.

Naturally, the villains’ gazes turned toward me. Judging by their reactions, they still did not know who I was.

Blood Wolf Saber asked me,

“Brat, who are you?”

Instead of answering, I said to him,

“I heard you were originally someone who walked his own path. I didn’t expect you to come kill someone at another’s instigation.”

Blood Wolf Saber, struck where it hurt, looked at me coldly. I did not know how he had come to be here, but I did know that he was a man who had lived for nothing but pride.

“I asked who you are.”

“Geom Mugeuk.”

“Geom Mugeuk?”

Then the eldest of the Three Lords of the Blood Road recognized me from behind.

“The Heavenly Demon’s second son.”

His expression, which had been calm until now, instantly twisted.

“Damn it! That damned bastard! He drove us into a place where the Heavenly Demon’s bloodline is present.”

At that, the second took up his words.

“He’ll probably insist he didn’t know he had come together with the Evil Smiling Demon. But it’s not as if we’re in a situation where we can withdraw either, so this is troublesome.”

I did not know the reason, but it seemed they too had been driven into a situation where they absolutely had to kill the Evil Smiling Demon. Well, if not for that, they would not have dared think of killing a Demon Venerable.

On the other hand, Blood Wolf Saber showed no fear at all even after learning my identity.

“You’re running your mouth because you trust your father. Do you think I fear your father?”

This too was the result of his pride being triggered. He was a man who lived by pride and died by pride. But how could that be called pride?

“A person with nothing to protect naturally has nothing to fear.”

At my words, his momentum surged. In a situation where he looked ready to draw his saber at once, I cut off the flow of that momentum and retreated behind the Evil Smiling Demon.

Blood Wolf Saber did not draw his saber recklessly. Since he would not yet know my true ability, he was likely being wary of the Evil Smiling Demon.

I openly asked the Evil Smiling Demon so everyone could hear.

“The person behind this is someone capable of mobilizing people like them, correct?”

“As you can see, yes.”

“Then why did he send them instead of stepping forward himself?”

“Most likely… because of you, Second Young Master.”

“Because of me?”

“He is hoping that one of them will kill you, Second Young Master. Then the responsibility for killing you will fall on that person.”

“A very cowardly bastard, then.”

I looked at the villains and said,

“Well then, who will be the first to fall for that cowardly intent?”

For a moment, silence flowed. Even if this was the Valley of Villains, there was fear in the name of the Heavenly Demon. If Father truly became enraged, he could attack the Valley of Villains as well. The reason he had left it alone until now was because that place was an even greater burden to the Murim Alliance.

The villains began exchanging sound transmissions among themselves. On the surface, they appeared to be bickering and eager to tear one another apart, but they were villains who had been worn smooth by the jianghu. Because they handled matters where their lives were at stake, they were extremely cautious. It was also the reason they had survived until now despite their countless evil deeds.

After a moment, the Paradise Enchantress stepped forward with a bewitching smile in her eyes.

“Little brother, you truly should come out with me. How could such an esteemed person get tangled up with these filthy villains?”

The instant I saw her eyes, I could feel that she had resolved to kill me. It seemed the mastermind close at hand was more frightening to her now than the Heavenly Demon far away.

The Paradise Enchantress lightly fluttered her fan.

“Little brother, shall we go out?”

The moment a vivid crimson energy flowed from the fan, an aura thick with bewitchment wrapped around me. She had used the Soul-Bewitching Art on me. It was the Soul-Bewitching Art of a woman who had plundered the inner energy of countless martial artists until now.

The instant a crimson light settled in my eyes, the Paradise Enchantress shouted at the Evil Smiling Demon,

“If you move, the Second Young Master dies!”

The Evil Smiling Demon did not budge. In truth, even if she had not warned him, he would not have moved. He was certain that I had killed the Soul-Bewitching Demon Venerable, so how could I fail to handle the Paradise Enchantress’s Soul-Bewitching Art? He must have trusted me that much.

Thinking that I had completely fallen under the Soul-Bewitching Art and lost my reason, the Paradise Enchantress approached me and placed her palm against my dantian.

“Shall I have a taste of my little brother’s fresh inner energy?”

Whoooooong!

The sound of inner energy being drawn from the dantian rang out.

The Paradise Enchantress shouted in a voice full of ecstasy.

“It has been my lifelong wish to suck dry the Heavenly Demon’s vital essence! Since I’m eating his bloodline, I have achieved half that wish now.”

The Paradise Enchantress’s expression changed from moment to moment, containing joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure. The Evil Smiling Demon, and all the other villains in the hall, simply watched the sight.

The youngest of the Three Lords of the Blood Road ran his mouth at the Evil Smiling Demon.

“You cold-blooded bastard! Even as the Heavenly Demon’s bloodline suffers, you just stand there watching.”

At that, the Evil Smiling Demon calmly asked them,

“You lot. Can you handle what comes after?”

“We can simply hide in the Valley of Villains. We’ll burn your corpses and throw them away, and no one will know it was our doing. Even if it is revealed, do you think your Demon Cult will truly bear such heavy sacrifices to attack the Valley of Villains?”

At the third’s answer, the Evil Smiling Demon said nothing more and simply watched as the Paradise Enchantress plundered my inner energy.

And a moment later.

Thud.

The Paradise Enchantress collapsed where she stood, crumpling to the floor.

Startled, the eldest of the Three Lords of the Blood Road examined her.

“Old hag, what’s wrong?”

The eldest, after checking her, shouted in shock.

“She’s dead! She died because her inner energy was exhausted!”

At that moment, my eyes flashed open.

“Ah, I’m full! She was damn troublesome, but she was very delicious.”

I had instead absorbed all of her inner energy.

I had deliberately pretended to be caught, but sorcery does not work on me. In particular, arts of the Soul-Bewitching type absolutely do not work.

Recently, I had gained insight into martial learning, and on top of that, I had the Blood-Eye Essence, the Heavenly Demon Body-Protecting Art, and the Heavenly Vein Strengthening Art. From the beginning, it had been impossible for her to take inner energy from my body.

In the end, the Paradise Enchantress met a miserable death by having the very method she had used all her life to plunder men turned back on her.

As I stored the inner energy I had gained from her in my dantian, I looked at Divine Lord Yama with eyes that had deepened further and said,

“What are you staring at? Aren’t you going to write our big sister’s name in your ledger?”

Chapter 146: No Matter How Urgent It Is.
----------------------------------------
Divine Lord Yama opened the Ledger of Slaughter.

“You knew. You knew that Second Young Master would not fall to her.”

Of course Extreme Evil Soma had trusted me.

Extreme Evil Soma’s eyes were smiling within the eyeholes of his mask. Seeing us calmly looking at each other and smiling, the eldest of the Three Lords of the Blood Road revealed his fury.

Originally, this should have been a fight I yielded to Extreme Evil Soma. But now was a situation where no variables could be permitted. We had to deal with them without taking injuries if possible, then leave this place. The true enemy was waiting for us outside.

Extreme Evil Soma also guessed my intent, so he willingly yielded this fight to me.

“I will.”

There were still four left besides Blood Wolf Saber, yet Extreme Evil Soma answered with confidence.

The moment I finished speaking, I charged toward Blood Wolf Saber.

Blood Wolf Saber drew his straight saber.

Though he had been suppressed in momentum at the start of the fight, Blood Wolf Saber was not a man with a false reputation. His saber art was fast, precise, and powerful.

His saber came flying in with enough force to break my sword.

When sword and saber clashed, there was no ringing clang, but thunderous booms. Inner force was infused into both sword and saber, turning it into a contest of internal power. The shame of having been struck at his sore spot rode upon his saber.

He hammered, and hammered, and hammered again.

He pressed me like a madman. If it had been any other martial artist, their sword would already have broken, or their wrist would have snapped.

But I blocked, and blocked, and blocked again.

Beyond the colliding sword and saber, I saw his expression change from moment to moment. The composure he had shown at the start, when he thought he had seized the initiative, gradually turned into impatience. His wrist was likely beginning to ache.

Now, slowly, our positions began to change.

I became the one hammering. The Black Demon Sword began to strike down on his saber. It was not a contest of dazzling techniques, but the very contest of inner force he had intended, and I drove him into it.

Because I struck down with my sword so quickly, he could not dodge, nor could he unleash another technique.

Boom! Boom! Boom! Boom!

Just then, amid the heavy impacts, a wretched scream mingled with the blows.

“Kuaaaargh!”

His wrist, overpowered in inner force, had broken.

But my sword did not stop.

On the next move, his saber, unable to receive inner force, broke, and on the move after that, his body was cut in a long vertical line.

“Wasn’t this the life you wanted? To die fighting someone stronger.”

But I saw it. The resentment and regret reflected in his eyes at the final moment. Yes, words were easy, but truly living such a life could not have been easy.

Blood Wolf Saber toppled forward as blood sprayed in a straight line from the crown of his head to his navel. He had spent his whole life forcing duels on others, and in the end, he died by receiving back the very method he had used.

Divine Lord Yama and the Three Lords of the Blood Road watched this in silence. It was partly because of Extreme Evil Soma, but also because they had found no chance to interfere in this brute-force contest.

They likely had not expected Blood Wolf Saber to lose to me. After all, a head-on contest of inner force was Blood Wolf Saber’s specialty.

I said again to Divine Lord Yama,

“Did you write it down? Blood Wolf Saber’s name too?”

Blood Wolf Saber had died before his eyes, but he was not frightened in the least.

When he stepped toward me, the eldest of the Three Lords of the Blood Road stopped him.

“Madman. Your opponent is over there.”

The eldest of the Three Lords of the Blood Road intended to kill me and avenge the Blissful Enchantress.

With my blood-dripping sword lowered, I walked toward them. Naturally, Extreme Evil Soma faced Divine Lord Yama.

At Extreme Evil Soma’s question, Divine Lord Yama shouted in a ringing voice,

“I am the envoy sent by the King of Hell. The King of Hell seeks you!”

Puaang! Kwaang!

Divine Lord Yama’s palm strike collided with Extreme Evil Soma’s Demonic Extreme Berserk Palm.

The aftermath sent a fierce wind rushing over us, and my fight with the Three Lords of the Blood Road began as well.

The three men charged at me at the same time.

The eldest’s sword aimed for my face, the second’s for my chest, and the third’s for my legs.

Clang! Clang! Claang!

I knocked away the incoming swords almost simultaneously. I was fast. No, I had to be fast. Their attacks were at a speed where, if I was not fast, some part of me would inevitably be pierced.

The directions of their thrusts kept changing. This time the eldest aimed for my chest, the second for my stomach, and the third for my face. The next time, it changed again.

It seemed their order of attack had already been set through dozens, hundreds of practices and experiences. This combined assault was perfect, having thoroughly studied the opponent’s mind. Truly, if it had not been me, I would have been stabbed several times by this merciless attack.

Clangclangclangclangclang!

I was continuously pushed back as I knocked away their attacks.

Then, seizing an opening, I attacked.

When the Black Demon Sword stabbed toward the eldest, the second joined in defending, while the third thrust at me.

Because they had fought together all their lives, though their bodies were three, they fought as if their minds were one. It was like fighting a monster with three heads and six arms. They were far more difficult opponents than Blood Wolf Saber, whom I had fought earlier. I was certain. Of the four villains who had come today, they were the most troublesome to face.

Four swords wove together, moving above and below. An exchange continued in which not even an inch of error was allowed.

I had no intention of dragging this fight out. That was why I thought of one method I had never used until now.

At the very moment they were pressing me—

Ssssst.

The startled second hurriedly looked around. The eldest and third had suddenly vanished, and he was standing alone with me in a field.

Through the Space-Time Transposition Art, I had moved only the second to a new space.

To the eyes of the eldest and third left behind, our forms must have vanished in an instant.

The second shouted at me,

“Is this an illusion art? Cowardly!”

“Well, by your standards, I suppose one-on-one is cowardly.”

I charged toward him. Even the three of them together had failed to kill me; alone, he could not possibly face me.

Outside, the eldest and third were looking around in shock.

If only their opponent had disappeared, that would have been one thing, but even the second had vanished with me.

At that moment, the second’s corpse appeared as if dropping from thin air. The instant the third was flustered by the corpse that had suddenly appeared before his eyes—

Swish! Thunk!

The Black Demon Sword pierced through the corpse’s armpit and stabbed into the third’s heart. Considering their skill, it was an utterly empty death, but their opponent was none other than me, who had incorporated the Space-Time Transposition Art into actual combat.

Without even letting out a single scream, the third also collapsed.

I thought the eldest would lose his reason and charge in like a madman.

But what he chose was escape. He tried to break through one wall of the inn and flee, but in a flash, I blocked his path with Flicker Step.

Startled, he turned again and fled. He threw the Blissful Enchantress’s corpse, which lay on the floor, at me. He had intended to kill me to avenge her, and yet—

“No matter how urgent it is, that’s not right, is it?”

“Shut up, you bastard!”

As though he judged the fight had already turned against him, he went berserk in order to live. He shouted and swung his sword like a madman. But there was no way such struggles would work.

Before even five moves had passed—

Thuk!

The Black Demon Sword pierced his heart, and even faster than that, cut off his wrist.

Thud.

In the fallen hand was a pouch. It was a poison pouch he had meant to scatter at me. The instant he was stabbed by my sword, he had tried to spray poison at me and perish together.

I had known from the start that they were such vicious men. I simply thought their end had come far too late. After committing all manner of evil their entire lives, they only died now, in their later years. If I had not regressed, they would not even have died here.

Isn’t this too unfair? That is why everyone laments that even the heavens are indifferent.

When my fight ended, Extreme Evil Soma’s fight had ended as well.

Divine Lord Yama was already dead, his forehead pierced by the Blood Calamity Finger, his face buried in his own ledger. The blood flowing out soaked his Ledger of Slaughter.

“You spent your whole life pretending to be the envoy of the King of Hell, but when the King of Hell actually sees you, he’ll say this: Who are you? When did I ever send you?”

At my words, Extreme Evil Soma laughed and asked,

“Are you hurt anywhere?”

“I’m fine. What about you, Lord Soma?”

“I’m fine as well.”

Though it might have seemed we had won easily, in truth, they were powerful enemies against whom it would not have been strange if either of us had died.

But we handled it well, and once again passed safely through a crisis. With him, unintentionally, I kept crossing the boundaries of life and death like this.

“Your skills have improved again while I wasn’t watching. Just how strong do you intend to become?”

“I intend to go all the way to the end.”

“If you learn the Nine Flames Demonic Art on top of this, there will be no one under heaven who can face you.”

I truly hoped so. Truly, sincerely, I hoped no one would be my match.

Before going outside, I placed money on the counter at the entrance of the inn. It was enough to repair the damaged inn and buy new furnishings. It was money for the innkeeper, who must have fled somewhere. What happened today had likely been forced upon him.

“Now, this sight no longer seems strange.”

“As you know, the demonic path I pursue is a demonic path that does not break tables.”

“Do you believe we can become good people, Second Young Master?”

“I do not wish for us to become good people.”

“Then?”

“I am trying to uphold at least what must be upheld. Shouldn’t we at least become human first, and only above that can there be the demonic path, the orthodox path, or the heretical path? That is all I want.”

Extreme Evil Soma stared at me silently for a moment. I could not know what thoughts he was looking at me with, but at the very least, it was certain that he was gradually becoming accustomed to the person I was.

“Let’s go out.”

“Let’s.”

Together, we walked out of the inn.

Outside, there were no passersby at all. The street was truly empty.

Before us stood a man wearing a white mask.

He was merely standing there, yet I felt an overwhelming presence from him. A presence no less than that of the Sword Emperor Baek Manggi.

I could tell. This man was the fake who had impersonated Extreme Evil Soma, and at the same time, the mastermind behind this trap.

“Have you forgotten your manners now that you’ve been associating with those of the demonic path?”

Extreme Evil Soma stared at him for a moment with complicated eyes, then spoke in a calm tone.

“I greet Senior Martial Uncle.”

He was someone I also knew. He was Liang Qiji, the senior disciple-brother of Extreme Evil Soma’s master. Before my regression, when I had formed a connection with Extreme Evil Soma, he had once told me about this senior martial uncle.

Liang Qiji spoke to Extreme Evil Soma in a commanding tone.

“Take off your mask.”

Chapter 147: Who on Earth Did He Join Hands With.
-------------------------------------------------
“I refuse.”

Geugak Soma flatly declined.

The fact that he could say something so shameless after having tried to release the villains of the Valley of Villains to kill Geugak Soma told me exactly what kind of man he was.

“What is this paltry mask, anyway!”

Yang Cheogi took off his mask. A wrinkled old man appeared, and he was truly an ugly wretch. His face was far too much of a contrast to Geugak Soma’s handsome face that I had seen before my regression.

Soma, thank you!”

I was startled. I had not imagined that he would act like this.

Rather than having brought them here to kill us, he had brought them here to torment Geugak Soma. Since they were wearing masks, I could not tell their ages, but judging by their bearing, there were many young experts among them.

What choice would Geugak Soma make?

If they charged at us to kill us, I too would have no choice but to act. They were a sect of the Evil Path, but they were Geugak Soma’s own sect. Could I kill them freely? And how would Geugak Soma respond?

I glared at Yang Cheogi. The absolute evil I spoke of meant precisely people like him. Not someone forced into an unavoidable choice, but someone with the malicious intent to deliberately break another person’s heart, someone who used the disciples of his sect as sacrifices without the slightest pang of conscience. You will surely die by my hand.

Just then, Geugak Soma spoke in a ringing voice.

Though I left the main sect and entrusted myself to the Divine Cult, I am the chief disciple of the late former sect master. In life, the sect master did not expel me, so as a legitimate disciple of the White Mask Sect, I command you. All of you, withdraw!”

The disciples of the White Mask Sect looked at one another and exchanged glances.

Yang Cheogi shouted,

“What are you doing? Kill them at once!”

Geugak Soma shouted even louder.

At that moment, someone released a finger wind.

Piiing.

Geugak Soma recognized at a glance that the man who had fired the finger wind was his senior martial brother.

In the gazes that met in midair were memories and longing from their childhood.

Because they had heard everything I had said earlier to Yang Cheogi, they knew what kind of situation this was.
